title: Quantization performance & quality tradeoff benchmarks (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ, kernels)
content:
Summary:
This note summarizes end-to-end performance and quality tradeoff experiments for quantized inference variants we are evaluating for the serving runtime. We benchmarked INT8 (symmetric per-channel), FP8 (e4m3-style), and two post-training quant schemes (GPTQ, AWQ) across kernel variants (baseline cuBLAS GEMM + reference attention, fused Triton kernels, and our new tiled KV-cache kernels). Goal is to produce practical recommendations for which quantization+kernel combos to ship for 7B and 13B-class models and to identify where kernel work still gives most ROI.

Key takeaways (short):
- For 7B-class models, AWQ + fused kernels gives the best latency/quality tradeoff in our tests: ~1.9x throughput vs fp16 and <1% relative quality regressions on coding/completion evals.
- For 13B-class models, GPTQ-INT8 provides substantial memory savings and ~1.4x throughput gain, but quality regressions are more model-dependent (perplexity +0.6-1.8).
- FP8 (e4m3) delivered lower quantization-induced quality loss than INT8 for some attention-heavy variants, and on H100 it enables higher sustained throughput vs INT8 due to faster FP8 GEMM kernels; however kernel maturity on A100 is still lacking.
- Kernel selection matters: fused attention + KV-cache tiled GEMM produced the largest latency gains (p95 down ~30-45%) compared to stacked naive GEMM + reference attention.

Experiment setup:
- Models: Llama-2-13B (hf converted), MPT-7B, Falcon-7B (used only for cross-check).
- Quant methods: INT8 (per-channel symmetric), FP8 e4m3 (simulated where hardware support missing), GPTQ (8-bit per-tensor/algo specific), AWQ (per-channel asymmetric with outlier handling).
- Kernels tested: baseline-cuBLAS (fp16 fallback), fused-triton-attn (our experimental fused attention kernel v0.3), tiled-kv-cache (prototype tiled matmul + kv cache layout), vendor-FP8 (H100-optimized GEMM).
- Hardware: A100-40GB, H100-80GB (single-GPU measurements).
- Workload: mixture of chat-style prompts (avg seq len 512 request+response cap 1024), batch sizes {1,4,8}, steady-state stream for throughput, cold-start for first-token latency.
- Metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95 first-token latency, memory footprint (model+kv cache), perplexity on WikiText103, pass@1 on code eval (HumanEval-ish subset), and human-rated quality for a 200-sample prompt set (A/B between baseline fp16 and quant variant).

Profiling methodology & notes:
- Used nvprof/nvtx and Nsight Systems to capture kernel timelines. Macro profiling measured time spent in GEMM vs attention vs memory copies.
- Observed common bottlenecks: memory-bound GEMMs for INT8 when using non-fused kernels, attention kernel overhead when sequence length > 512 without fused attention, and host-to-device staging cost for large KV-cache updates.
- Collected kernel hotlist: cublasLtMatmul (fp16/fp32), custom_triton_fused_attn, tiled_gemm_kernel, kv_cache_update_kernel, fp8_gemm_vendor. These names map to our telemetry counters for per-route breakdowns.

Representative results (selected):
- MPT-7B, batch=1, seq=512:
  - fp16 baseline: tokens/sec 420, p50 95ms, p95 220ms, model mem 12.2GB
  - INT8-GPTQ + baseline kernels: tokens/sec 520 (+24%), p50 82ms, p95 210ms, mem 7.8GB, perplexity +0.9
  - AWQ + fused kernels: tokens/sec 800 (+90%), p50 52ms, p95 120ms, mem 8.0GB, perplexity +0.4, human A/B preference: 48% prefer quant vs fp16 (stat. tie)
  - FP8 (vendor kernel on H100): tokens/sec 920 (+119% vs fp16), p50 46ms, p95 100ms, mem 9.0GB, perplexity +0.3 (note: limited to H100)

- Llama-2-13B, batch=1, seq=512:
  - fp16 baseline: tokens/sec 180, p50 210ms, p95 520ms, mem 24.6GB
  - INT8-GPTQ + tiled kernels: tokens/sec 250 (+39%), p50 160ms, p95 420ms, mem 14.9GB, perplexity +1.1
  - AWQ + fused kernels: tokens/sec 325 (+81%), p50 120ms, p95 300ms, mem 15.6GB, perplexity +1.6 (some failure modes on long-range coherence)
  - FP8: not tested end-to-end on A100 due to missing vendor kernels; simulated FP8 matmul shows potential but real kernel needed for reliable latency numbers.

Quality observations:
- GPTQ often introduces brittle failure modes on tokens that depend on outlier weights. For code-generation tasks GPTQ sometimes loses variable naming consistency (observed on ~3% of samples).
- AWQ's adaptive outlier handling reduces those failure cases; on 7B AWQ moved quality delta to <1% on human-rated prompts.
- FP8 consistently has lower perplexity degradation when supported by hardware kernels versus simulated FP8 via fp16 emulation.

Kernel-level profiling insights:
- Fused attention reduces context-switch overhead and memory traffic: attention time contribution falls from ~27% to ~12% on average with fused kernels for seq 512.
- INT8-GEMM suffers from reduced arithmetic intensity on A100 when kernels are non-optimized (memory-bandwidth bound). Custom tiled_gemm with half-accumulation improved utilization and closed the gap by ~18% throughput.
- FP8 vendor kernels on H100 benefit from native tensor core support—end-to-end throughput is bounded by KV-cache writes for long sequences, not GEMM.

Recommendations (practical):
- 7B-class production: ship AWQ + fused kernels as the default quantized profile for hosted API and Dedicated. Falls back to fp16 for routes with strict quality SLOs.
- 13B-class production: offer GPTQ-INT8 as a cost-optimized profile behind a quality-warning flag; prefer AWQ where latency is priority and model behavior acceptable after eval.
- Prioritize engineering on: (1) fused attention + tiled KV-cache kernels for A100, (2) vendor FP8 paths for H100 (acquire kernel licenses), (3) robust quant-aware eval suites (automated prompt sets) to catch brittle failure modes.

Open issues / TODOs:
- Run CI-quality sweep across 10 largest customer prompt sets to measure real-world regressions (owner: Aditi).
- Implement FP8 vendor kernel on A100 or validate emulation costs in production (owner: Michael).
- Improve GPTQ outlier handling and add unit tests reproducing the code-gen failure patterns (owner: Samira).
- Add telemetry counters for 'quantization-mode' per-request to correlate customer regressions in console.

Notes to self (drafty):
- Need to standardize how we report "perplexity delta" vs human A/B ratings - customers care more about hallucinations than small perplexity changes.
- Save raw Nsight traces for the runs labeled "2024-10-22-awq-fused" and attach to the confluence page for kernel dev.
